Elaine: Quick note after the RFC walkthrough  we need a pragmatic contract for handing off in-flight streaming responses when we hedge or failover to a different upstream. Primary worries: out-of-order tokens and how we charge customers for partially delivered streams.

Ravi: Two lightweight primitives I like: (1) monotonic sequence included in each token frame (`X-GW-Seq`), (2) a short opaque resume nonce (`Resume-Nonce`) emitted at commit points. New upstreams start at `seq = last_committed + 1`.

Tom: Agree on seq + resume token. Operationally we should avoid checkpointing every N tokens expensive. Emit resume nonces only at semantic boundaries (sentence/paragraph) or when we actually switch upstreams.

Elaine: UX for clients? If we keep all dedupe server-side, SDKs don't need changes. That seems preferable for rollout. Gateway can maintain a small per-request seen-seq window and drop duplicates before delivering.

Ravi: That works. But add a short id for each message frame (`msg_id`) so dedupe is O(1) rather than scanning seq ranges. Gateway assigns `msg_id` when it first receives frames from upstream.

Tom: For resume state transfer, propose a tiny control RPC: `GET /resume-state?req_id=<id>` returning "{ \"last_committed_seq\": 1234, \"resume_nonce\": \"b64...\" }". New upstream fetches that before resuming. Keep state TTL short (30s).

Elaine: Example resume flow (high level):
1) Client starts streaming -> gateway proxies to Upstream A.
2) Gateway emits `checkpoint` frame at sentence boundary: `seq=42`, `resume_nonce=abc`.
3) Upstream A stalls or is slow; gateway starts Upstream B hedged attempt. B asks control-plane for resume-state and starts from seq=43.
4) Gateway suppresses any token frames with `msg_id` it has already delivered.

Ravi: Billing rule recommendation: bill only for committed tokens (last checkpointed seq). Still track attempted tokens internally for cost analysis (`metrics.stream.attempt.tokens`). External billing uses `metrics.stream.committed.tokens`.

Tom: Implementation note: commit log is ephemeral in the proxy (in-memory map keyed by `req_id` -> last_committed_seq + resume_nonce) with TTL and small memory cap. On failover the new proxy instance will call control-plane RPC if it doesn't have the entry locally.

Elaine: Observability/eventing: emit these events for each request: `stream.attempt.started`, `stream.checkpoint`, `stream.attempt.abandoned`, `stream.committed`. Include fields: req_id, last_committed_seq, attempt_id, upstream_id, consumed_tokens. These feed billing and SLO dashboards.

Ravi: Edge case: partial token frames (e.g., token emitted in pieces). We need seq/ids at the frame granularity downstream, otherwise dedupe can cut tokens in half. Recommend frames correspond to server-sent chunks (not characters). SDK teams can reassemble on client.

Tom: Rollout plan: behind feature flag `edge_midstream_resume_v2`. Canary to 5% next Monday. infra-bot please schedule deploy.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary scheduled for edge-proxy v1.12.1 on 2025-06-02T04:00:00Z. Feature flag: `edge_midstream_resume_v2`.

Elaine: Approve decision? (A) seq + resume-nonce checkpoints at semantic boundaries or upstream switch, (B) gateway-side dedupe with `msg_id`, (C) ephemeral commit log + resume RPC, (D) billing = committed tokens only.

Ravi: :+1:

Tom: :+1: I'll PR the control RPC proto and the proxy-side in-memory commit log.

Elaine: I'll write the short follow-up RFC with sample frame formats and the event schema for billing.
